question: If I work while I'm incarcerated, in a prison job or on work release, how is my pay set, what can the state deduct from my earnings and in what order, and what do I get back when I'm released?

gold_sections.why: Prison-industry pay: the authority's director (its chief administrative officer, hired by the board under 2808(e)) adopts a compensation schedule based on quantity and quality of work, capped at one-half the state minimum wage, credited to the inmate's account.
The Prison Industry Authority is now the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Authority; references to either mean the same body.

The only statute on ordinary (non-industry) prison job pay: prisoners doing productive labor outside the authority's programs 'may be compensated in like manner' from appropriated or other department funds; every able-bodied prisoner must work; escape forfeits earnings to the Inmate Welfare Fund.
The only statutory hourly rate: $7.25 an hour for incarcerated hand crew members while assigned to an active fire incident.
Pay in the Article 5 camp program (fire and conservation camps, 2717, 2780): a daily rate the director may fix, with the road-camp deductions of 2762 and a cap on net pay authorized by regulation.

Highway road camps (and, through 2782, camp deductions by regulation): a daily rate, with each convict's account debited for camp maintenance and commissary drawings, never transport or guarding, plus an add-on of up to 10 percent.

Joint venture (private-employer) jobs: wages comparable to the employer's non-inmate workers (or local wages), deductions capped at 80 percent of gross and limited to taxes, room and board, 5-20 percent restitution/victim funds, and family support.
Defines joint venture program and joint venture employer (contracts with the Director of Corrections to employ inmate labor).
The pay rule for state restitution centers: an offender may not take a job paying less than local rates for similar work.

Cobey Work Furlough Law for county jail sentences: prevailing-wage employment; the administrator may collect earnings (a prior levy or prior request wins) and pays board and expenses, an allocable administration share and dependents' support, then (with consent) debts; balance paid at discharge.

Counties may not impose a work furlough program administrative fee, and private work furlough operators may not impose administrative or application fees, which puts the 1208(e) administration share in doubt.

Restitution deductions from wages and trust account deposits: minimum 20 percent (or the balance) up to 50 percent; restitution order collected before the restitution fine; county-jail version is discretionary; collection may continue against parolees.
Condemned inmates must work, and 70 percent (or the balance) of their wages and trust deposits goes to restitution.

State restitution centers (work release in the state system): wages less taxes paid to the department, work costs reimbursed, then thirds to center costs, restitution (then court costs and attorney fees, then crime prevention), and the offender's savings paid at release.
All sums due for labor are paid on discharge; on parole they are paid as the director prescribes.

Release payment of $200 for each prisoner, which the department may limit for prisoners who served less than six consecutive months where not necessary for rehabilitation; not paid on release to another state or federal custody.
Inmate funds are held in trust and interest is credited to individual inmate trust accounts.
County boards of supervisors may credit jail prisoners who perform work assignments with a sum the board sets.

nuggets.text: Prison-industry pay follows a compensation schedule adopted by the director of the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Authority, based on the quantity and quality of work, never more than one-half the state minimum wage (unless the code says otherwise), and credited to the inmate's account.
nuggets.quote: the director shall adopt and maintain a compensation schedule for inmate employees. That compensation schedule shall be based on quantity and quality of work performed and shall be required for its performance, but in no event shall that compensation exceed one-half the minimum wage provided in Section 1182 of the Labor Code, except as otherwise provided in this code. This compensation shall be credited to the account of the inmate.

nuggets.text: Prisoners doing productive labor outside the authority's work programs (ordinary prison jobs) may be paid 'in like manner'; the statute sets no rate, and the pay comes from legislative appropriations or other department funds as the Director of Finance directs.
nuggets.quote: Prisoners not engaged on work programs under the jurisdiction of the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Authority, but who are engaged in productive labor outside of such programs may be compensated in like manner. The compensation of the prisoners shall be paid either out of funds appropriated by the Legislature for that purpose or out of such other funds available to the Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation for expenditure, as the Director of Finance may direct.

nuggets.text: Incarcerated hand crew members are paid $7.25 an hour while assigned to an active fire incident, a rate reviewed annually.
nuggets.quote: incarcerated individual hand crew members shall be paid an hourly wage equal to seven dollars and twenty-five cents ($7.25) while assigned to an active fire incident. The wage rate shall be reviewed annually.

nuggets.text: For prisoners in the Article 5 camp program (fire and conservation camps), the director may fix a daily rate of pay, may by regulation authorize the same deductions taken at road camps under 2762, and may by regulation cap the net amount a prisoner receives.
nuggets.quote: The director may fix a daily rate to be expended for such convict labor, and when so fixed, the agency shall monthly set aside funds to the director to pay for such labor, and where no funds are available from the agency the director may set aside the department's own funds to pay for such labor. The director, by regulation, may authorize any or all deductions to be made from the pay due convicts as provided for convicts at road camps under Section 2762. The director, by regulation, may also fix the maximum amount, over and above all deductions, that a convict may receive.

nuggets.text: In a joint venture program with an outside employer, pay must be comparable to what that employer pays non-inmate employees for similar work, or, if it has none, to local wages for similar work.
nuggets.quote: shall be comparable to wages paid by the joint venture employer to non-inmate employees performing similar work for that employer. If the joint venture employer does not employ such non-inmate employees in similar work, compensation shall be comparable to wages paid for work of a similar nature in the locality in which the work is to be performed.

nuggets.text: A restitution center offender may not take a job whose pay or conditions are below those for similar work in the locality.
nuggets.quote: The offender shall not be allowed to take employment if the rate of pay or other conditions of employment are less than those paid or provided for work of a similar nature in the locality in which the work is performed.

nuggets.text: County work furlough employment must pay at least the prevailing wage for similar work in the area, under prevailing working conditions.
nuggets.quote: shall be at a wage at least as high as the prevailing wage for similar work in the area where the work is performed and in accordance with the prevailing working conditions in that area

nuggets.text: Joint venture deductions are set by the Director of Corrections, may not total more than 80 percent of gross wages, and are limited to taxes, reasonable room and board, 5 to 20 percent of gross wages for restitution fines or victim-compensation funds, and family support under statute, court order or the prisoner's agreement (a capped set with no priority among the items).
nuggets.quote: Such wages shall be subject to deductions, as determined by the Director of Corrections, which shall not, in the aggregate, exceed 80 percent of gross wages and shall be limited to the following: (1) Federal, state, and local taxes. (2) Reasonable charges for room and board, which shall be remitted to the Director of Corrections. (3) Any lawful restitution fine or contributions to any fund established by law to compensate the victims of crime of not more than 20 percent, but not less than 5 percent, of gross wages, which shall be remitted to the Director of Corrections for disbursement. (4) Allocations for support of family pursuant to state statute, court order, or agreement by the prisoner.

nuggets.text: If a state prisoner owes a restitution fine, the Secretary must deduct at least 20 percent (or the balance owing, if less) and up to 50 percent from the prisoner's wages and trust account deposits, unless federal law prohibits it, and send it to the Victim Compensation Board; the same percentages apply to a victim restitution order.
nuggets.quote: the secretary shall deduct a minimum of 20 percent or the balance owing on the fine amount, whichever is less, up to a maximum of 50 percent from the wages and trust account deposits of a prisoner, unless prohibited by federal law

nuggets.text: When a prisoner owes both a restitution fine and a restitution order, the department collects the (victim) restitution order first.
nuggets.quote: If a prisoner has both a restitution fine and a restitution order from the sentencing court, the department shall collect the restitution order first

nuggets.text: For a condemned inmate who owes restitution, the Secretary deducts 70 percent (or the balance owing, if less) of wages and trust account deposits, whatever the source.
nuggets.quote: the Secretary of the Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation shall deduct 70 percent or the balance owing, whichever is less, from the condemned inmate's wages and trust account deposits, regardless of the source of the income

nuggets.text: At highway road camps (and at fire and conservation camps where the director adopts these deductions by regulation under 2782), each prisoner's account is debited monthly for a share of camp maintenance (food, medicine, medical attendance, staff, welfare facilities) and commissary drawings, never for transport or guarding; the director may cap net pay, and the department may add up to 10 percent to all debits.
nuggets.quote: Such account shall be debited monthly with the convict's proportionate share of expenses of camp maintenance, including the expenses for food, medicine, medical attendance, clerical and accounting personnel, and the expenses necessary to maintain care and welfare facilities such as camp hospital for first aid, barbershop and cobbler shop, and the convict's personal expenses covering his drawings from the commissary for clothing, toilet articles, candy, and other personal items. The charge for camp maintenance may be made at a standard rate determined by the department maintaining the camps to be adequate to cover expenses and shall be adjusted periodically at the discretion of the department as needs of the camp require. No charge shall be made against such account for the costs of transporting prisoners to and from prison and camp or for the expense of guarding prisoners, which items shall be paid by the Department of Corrections from appropriations made for the support of the department. The director, by regulation, may fix the maximum amount, over and above all deductions, that a convict may receive. The Department of Corrections, in computing the debits to be made to the convict's accounts, may add not to exceed 10 percent on all items.

nuggets.text: In a state restitution center, wages minus taxes are paid directly to the Department of Corrections, which first reimburses the offender's costs of keeping the job (transportation, tools or clothing, meals, union dues).
nuggets.quote: Wages earned by an offender, less any deductions for taxes, shall be paid directly to the Department of Corrections. (b) Wage moneys received by the department shall be used to reimburse the offender for costs directly associated with continued employment

nuggets.text: The remaining restitution-center wages are split into thirds: one-third to the department for operating the center, and one-third to restitution under the agreement or court order, which after restitution is paid goes to the prosecuting jurisdiction's court costs and attorney fees, and then to local crime prevention.
nuggets.quote: The remaining wages shall be distributed as follows: (1) One-third shall be transferred to the Department of Corrections to pay the costs of operating and maintaining the restitution center. (2) One-third shall be used to pay restitution pursuant to the agreement or court order. After the restitution is paid these moneys shall be paid to the jurisdiction which prosecuted the offender to defray the court costs and attorney fees incurred in the offender's prosecution. If all restitution, court costs and attorney fees are paid, these moneys shall be paid to the local jurisdiction for crime prevention.

nuggets.text: The county work furlough administrator may collect the prisoner's earnings, and the employer must send the wages on request; earnings already levied on under a writ of execution are not sent, unless the administrator's request came before the levy.
nuggets.quote: The earnings of the prisoner may be collected by the work furlough administrator, and it shall be the duty of the prisoner's employer to transmit the wages to the administrator at the latter's request. Earnings levied upon pursuant to writ of execution or in other lawful manner shall not be transmitted to the administrator. If the administrator has requested transmittal of earnings prior to levy, that request shall have priority.

nuggets.text: From work furlough earnings it collects, the administrator pays the prisoner's board and personal expenses, deducts the prisoner's allocable share of administration costs (or a lesser reasonable sum), and pays the support of dependents in an amount the administrator sets; the statute joins these with 'and' and does not rank them.
nuggets.quote: From the earnings the administrator shall pay the prisoner's board and personal expenses, both inside and outside the jail, and shall deduct so much of the costs of administration of this section as is allocable to the prisoner or if the prisoner is unable to pay that sum, a lesser sum as is reasonable, and, in an amount determined by the administrator, shall pay the support of the prisoner's dependents, if any.

nuggets.text: A county that runs work furlough may not impose a program administrative fee, and privately operated work furlough programs may not impose administrative or application fees.
nuggets.quote: A board of supervisors that implements programs identified in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) shall not impose a program administrative fee. (2) Privately operated electronic home detention programs pursuant to Section 1203.016 or 1203.018 or work furlough programs pursuant to Section 1208 shall not impose program administrative fees or application fees.

nuggets.text: Only after those payments, and only with the prisoner's consent, may the administrator pay preexisting debts; any balance is held and paid to the prisoner at discharge.
nuggets.quote: If sufficient funds are available after making the foregoing payments, the administrator may, with the consent of the prisoner, pay, in whole or in part, the preexisting debts of the prisoner. Any balance shall be retained until the prisoner's discharge. Upon discharge the balance shall be paid to the prisoner.

nuggets.text: The last third of restitution-center wages goes to a savings account for the offender's immediate family, work necessities or personal items, and whatever remains when the offender leaves the restitution center is paid to the offender.
nuggets.quote: One-third shall be placed in a savings account for the offender, to provide support for the offender's immediate family, to purchase items necessary for the offender's employment or to give to the offender to purchase personal accessories. Any moneys in the savings account or not expended pursuant to this paragraph at the time the offender is released from the restitution center shall be paid to the offender.

nuggets.text: An inmate paid for labor who is discharged gets all sums due on release; an inmate released on parole is paid as the director prescribes.
nuggets.quote: all sums due him shall be paid upon release. If an inmate is released on parole all sums due him shall be paid to the inmate as prescribed by the director.

nuggets.text: Each prisoner is also paid $200 on release (from available appropriations); by rule the department may limit or eliminate it for prisoners who served less than six consecutive months where it finds the payment unnecessary for rehabilitation, may pay it within the first 60 days, and may cancel the unpaid balance for a parolee who absconds; it is not paid on release to another state's or federal custody.
nuggets.quote: each prisoner upon his release shall be paid the sum of two hundred dollars ($200), from such appropriations that may be made available for the purposes of this section. The department may prescribe rules and regulations (a) to limit or eliminate any payments provided for in this section to prisoners who have not served for at least six consecutive months prior to their release in instances where the department determines that such a payment is not necessary for rehabilitation of the prisoner, (b) to establish procedures for the payment of the sum of two hundred dollars ($200) within the first 60 days of a prisoner's release, and (c) to eliminate any payment provided for in this section to a parolee who upon release has not been paid the entire amount prescribed by this section and who willfully absconds after release on parole, but before any remaining balance of the two hundred dollar ($200) release funds has been paid. The provisions of this section shall not be applicable if a prisoner is released to the custody of another state or to the custody of the federal government.

nuggets.text: Release does not end restitution: the Secretary (or, for a county jail term under 1170(h), the county's designated agency) may collect unpaid restitution fines from a parolee, unless federal law prohibits it.
nuggets.quote: either the secretary or, if a prisoner is punished by imprisonment in a county jail pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170, the agency designated by the board of supervisors in the county where the prisoner is incarcerated may collect from the parolee any moneys owing on the restitution fine amount, unless prohibited by federal law

State restitution center: taxes are withheld before the wages reach the department

answer: Prison-industry pay follows the industry authority director's schedule by work quantity and quality, capped at half the minimum wage [N1]; other jobs may be paid "in like manner," at no statutory rate [N2]. Fire hand crews earn $7.25 hourly on active fires [N3]; camp pay is a daily rate the director may fix, less regulatory deductions [N4] such as upkeep, food, medical and commissary debits plus up to 10 percent [N12]. Joint venture jobs pay comparable wages [N5], with deductions capped at 80 percent: taxes, room and board, 5-20 percent restitution, family support [N8]. Restitution-center jobs must pay local rates [N6]; county furlough, at least the prevailing wage [N7]. For restitution, the Secretary takes 20-50 percent of wages and trust deposits [N9] (70 percent on death row [N11]), victim restitution before the fine [N10]. Restitution-center wages, minus taxes, go to the department, which repays work costs [N13] and splits the rest in thirds: center costs; restitution (then court costs, then crime prevention) [N14]; and savings paid at release [N19]. A furlough administrator may collect your wages [N15] to pay board, expenses and dependents' support (an administration share is listed [N16], but administrative fees are banned [N17]), then consented debts; the balance is paid at discharge [N18]. At release you get all sums due (parolees as the director prescribes) [N20] plus $200, limitable for stays under six months if unneeded for rehabilitation, and not paid on release to other-state or federal custody [N21]. Restitution can still be collected on parole [N22].

version_flags: No gold section carries an effective-date heading in the downloaded corpus; 1208 is the version made operative July 1, 2021 (its subdivision (l)), and the $7.25 hand-crew wage in 2714 (repeated in 4019.2(c)) is treated as in force on 2026-10-10

CCP 704.090(a)'s $1,750 inmate trust account exemption is the statutory base amount: as an Article 3 exemption it is adjusted every three years under CCP 703.150(b) (on April 1, 2025, next April 1, 2028), so the figure in force on 2026-10-10 is the Judicial Council's published amount; the $325 restitution-judgment exemption in 704.090(b) is not adjusted
local_option: County boards of supervisors decide by ordinance whether to run a Cobey work furlough program and who serves as the work furlough administrator (1208(a)); the administrator may collect earnings, sets the dependents' support amount and may pay preexisting debts only with the prisoner's consent (1208(e)); 1208.2 bars counties and private operators from charging work furlough program administrative or application fees; for people serving county jail terms under 1170(h), the county's designated agency 'is authorized' (not required) to take 20-50 percent of wages and trust deposits for restitution (2085.5(b),(d)) and the county elects whether to keep collecting after release (2085.6, 2085.7); boards may credit jail prisoners who work with a sum they set (4019.3); on county industrial farms and road camps the board fixes daily credits of not more than $2 (prisoners with dependents) or $1 (others) per eight-hour day, the superintendent may credit less for lack of effort, the balance is paid at discharge, the prisoner may direct payment to dependents or creditors, and the sentencing court may order payment to dependents (4125-4127); joint county camps may pay up to $0.75 a day, charge unreturned tools against pay, and must pay dependents monthly (4222-4224); counties must keep a dispute process for hand-crew pay at county camps (4019.2(c)(3)).
notes: Scope: state prisoners (CDCR) first, then state restitution centers and county work furlough as work release. Ordering: the code has several explicit sequences, none general: 2085.5(g) (restitution order before the fine; counties too, 2085.5(h), 2085.6(d), 2085.7(d)); 6231 (taxes withheld, then work-cost reimbursement, then three concurrent thirds, with the restitution third running restitution, then court costs and attorney fees, then crime prevention); and 1208(e) (a prior levy or prior administrator request takes the wages first; board and expenses, administration share and dependents' support are joined by 'and' and not ranked among themselves; consented debts only 'after making the foregoing payments'; balance at discharge). 2717.8's four joint venture deductions are a capped set with no priority. 2085.5 applies the same 20-50 percent deduction to restitution fines (subd. (a)) and restitution orders (subd. (c)); the older 10 percent administrative fee is no longer in the text. 2717.8(3) limits restitution/victim-fund deductions from joint venture gross wages to 5-20 percent while 2085.5 sets 20-50 percent of wages and trust deposits generally; the code does not reconcile them (2700.1 cross-references both), and 2717.8 is the more specific rule for joint venture paychecks. 2085.5(j) exempts non-wage money spent on canteen food for family visits ($50/$70/$80 caps). Condemned inmates lose 70 percent (or the balance) of wages and deposits to restitution (2700.1). Forfeitures: earnings may be forfeited to the Inmate Welfare Fund on escape (2700(d)) or wilful rule violations in camps (2765, 2785). 2782 applies to the Article 5 camp program, which 2717 calls fire crews and 2780.6 calls the California Conservation Camp program; its deductions follow 2762 only as the director adopts them by regulation. 'The director' in 2811 is the authority's director, the chief administrative officer its board employs (2808(e)). Restitution centers (6220-6236) are statutory work release for state prisoners: the Director may establish them (6220), the court may order an eligible defendant placed there with a restitution order or agreement (6227), and eligibility excludes recent drug-sale, sex-registration, serious or violent felony histories and sentences over 60 months and requires employability (6228). 1208(e) still lists the allocable 'costs of administration' while 1208.2(b), which applies to 1208 work furlough (1208.2(a)(1)), forbids a 'program administrative fee' (and private programs' administrative or application fees); the reference treats the administration share as barred or at least contested, not as a routine deduction. Family support reaches prisoners' pay through joint venture allocations (2717.8(4)), work furlough (1208(e)), the restitution-center savings third (6231(b)(3)), and county farms and camps (4125-4127, 4224); no statute in the corpus deducts family support from ordinary state prison wages. After release, restitution fines and orders remain collectible from parolees (2085.5(e),(f),(i)) and under postrelease community supervision, mandatory supervision and after a county term (2085.6, 2085.7). Hand-crew pay disputes go to a CDCR or county administrative remedy process (4019.2(c)(2)-(3)). Joint venture participants cannot draw unemployment benefits from that work (2717.9). Trust account funds earn interest (5008) and are exempt from civil levy up to the CCP 704.090(a) amount ($1,750 statutory base, adjusted under 703.150), or $325 against restitution judgments (704.090(b)). The $200 release payment may be paid within 60 days of release under department rules and cancelled for a parolee who absconds before the balance is paid (2713.1). Medical visit fees are barred (5007.5).
